reviews.evidence: Diaz led off at DH against a Guardians bullpen game that Shawn Armstrong opened, as the model expected (slot 1). He went 2-for-5 with 3 Ks, and his two hits included a two-run HR in the 9th worth 6 TB. That's tail power, not a role change (NBC Sports).

Aranda batted 2nd as expected and went 3-for-4 with three singles and no extra-base hits, so 3 total bases came from singles alone. One single went for two runs after DeLauter misplayed it in right (WKYC recap). No missed role or lineup change found.

Bailey batted 7th as expected and went 1-for-4 with 0 K on 14 pitches in the Rays' 7-3 Game 4 win (CBS Sports). His role was normal and nothing changed. The model gave about a 50/50 chance either way and the single hit landed on the losing side.

Palacios batted 8th, as the model expected, against a CLE bullpen game that Shawn Armstrong opened after Friday's rainout (CBS lineups). He went 3-for-4. The 0.8-pt close move (fair 0.496 to 0.487) has no news behind it that I could find.

Simpson went 1-for-3. His one hit was a two-run triple off a Williams sweeper in the 4th, which cleared 1.5 by itself. The Rays had only 3 hits and 13 strikeouts in ALCS Game 3 (CBS recap), so the low-offense read held and a single rare extra-base hit decided the bet.

Tucker went 2-for-4 in LAD's 6-4 NLCS Game 4 loss to MIL (Bleacher Report/AP recaps). I found no injury, lineup or role change. The model itself put the under at only 42%, so 1+ hits was the likely outcome.

Per the ESPN recap, Ramírez batted 2nd as usual and went 2-for-3 with a walk in CLE's 3-2 ALCS Game 3 win. I found no change in role, lineup or injuries. The market made the over about a 64% favorite, so a 2-hit game was the likely outcome.

Turang batted 2nd and came up 4 times, with 0-2, 2 BB and 1 K in Milwaukee's 6-4 Game 4 win that finished the NLCS sweep (ESPN). The two walks left him only 2 at-bats. His role was intact, so this looks like ordinary variance.

Gavin Williams dominated in ALCS Game 3. He struck Walls out for his 9th K, and Tampa Bay managed only 3 hits. The model gave oppSp (0.48) zero weight (c_oppSp=0), and the over drifted from -102 to +116 by close.

Contreras played his usual role, went 1-4 with 2 K, and the over cashed. The price only moved from -179 to -167 (fair 0.600 to 0.585), and previews of NLCS Game 3 showed no injury, lineup or role news that would explain the move.

Previews (ESPN, Yahoo/Action, BetMGM) all listed the total at 7.5 with Gasser vs Snell. It slid to 7 by first pitch, and I found no injury, lineup or weather news behind the move. The over still won with 8 total runs (MIL 6-2 on 7th-inning homers).

Kwan went 2-for-5 leading off in ALCS Game 2, a 3-1 Rays win where Peralta allowed 4 hits (ESPN recap). Leadoff role and lineup were as expected. The under was a 37.7% shot and the market price (+149 close) agreed, so the over hitting was an ordinary result.

The total closed at 6.5 (-120), down from the 7 the model bet, and previews backed the under. Peralta, September's AL Pitcher of the Month, threw 6 scoreless innings with 6 K in a 3-1 game, so 4 runs fell far below the 7.45 projection.

Halpin went 1-for-3 batting 7th in ALCS Game 2, which CLE lost 3-1 at Tropicana Field (Baseball-Reference). The Over went from -118 to -105 at close for no reason I could find. My searches ran out before I found the TB starter or any lineup news.

The model's script factor of 0.715 cut Ramírez's mean from a 0.94 hits/game rate to 0.75, even though CLE was projected to win by 1.14. Batting 2nd, he got 5 AB and 3 hits as Cleveland totaled 14 hits in a 7-3 win (AP/WHEC). The script cut made the market's -182 Over look like value on the Under.

DeLauter batted in his usual spot and went 3-for-4 with a HR and a walk off Rays starter Drew Rasmussen as Cleveland got 14 hits in a 7-3 Game 1 win (ESPN). The line never moved and the inputs held up. A hit was already the ~60% outcome, and three hits is just the tail.

Bailey started at catcher, batting 7th, as the model expected. He went 2-for-4 off Rasmussen, including a game-tying solo HR in the 7th (SI recap). No role, lineup or injury change found, so a near coin-flip Under (55%) lost to normal variance.

AP recap: TB led 2-0 after the 1st, Rasmussen gave up 8 hits and solo HRs to DeLauter and Bailey, and Lowe's 2-run single in the 8th broke the tie. Cleveland's 5 relievers gave up 1 run in 5 IP. A close game decided late; no injury or lineup surprise found.

Pages batted 7th in CF as the model expected (Dodgers lineup on X). He went 0-for-2 with a walk and a strikeout in only 3 PA, while Henderson and Milwaukee's bullpen held LA down (CBS live blog). His role and inputs were right; the result was in the tail.

CBS Sports confirmed Hamilton started at 3B batting 9th vs. RHP Yamamoto, matching the model's slot 9. The over drifted from -108 to -101 near close for no reason we could find, and he went 2-for-3, so the bet won. The 1.6-point CLV loss looks like ordinary market noise.

Pratt faced ace Tarik Skubal, who was dominant early in a 2-1 low-scoring game. Pratt struck out in both of his at-bats (0-2, 2 K). His third plate appearance was a sacrifice bunt that didn't count as an at-bat, which left him fewer chances for a hit (ESPN/MLB.com recaps).

Freeman batted 2nd as the model expected (SI lineup) and went 1-for-4, so the over won. The price only drifted from -147 to -141, about 1 point of probability. That's normal noise before an ace start (Misiorowski, 1.80 ERA), and I found no injury or lineup news behind it.
